msrc19.title: Trends, Challenges, and Strategic Shifts in the Software Vulnerability Mitigation Landscape
msrc19.text: M. Miller (Microsoft Security Response Center). “Trends, Challenges, and Strategic Shifts in the Software Vulnerability Mitigation Landscape.” BlueHat IL, 2019. The source of the widely quoted figure that ~70% of the CVEs Microsoft assigns are memory-safety issues.

chromium.title: Memory safety (Chromium security documentation)
chromium.text: The Chromium Projects. “Memory safety.” Chromium security documentation, chromium.org. Reports that around 70% of Chromium's serious security bugs are memory-safety problems.

android22.title: Memory Safe Languages in Android 13
android22.text: J. Vander Stoep. “Memory Safe Languages in Android 13.” Google Security Blog, 2022. Reports memory-safety bugs falling as a share of Android's total vulnerabilities as new code moved to memory-safe languages.

astrauskas20.title: How Do Programmers Use Unsafe Rust?
astrauskas20.text: V. Astrauskas, C. Matheja, F. Poli, P. Müller, A. J. Summers. OOPSLA 2020 (PACMPL vol. 4).

evans20.title: Is Rust Used Safely by Software Developers?
evans20.text: A. N. Evans, B. Campbell, M. L. Soffa. ICSE 2020.

qin20.title: Understanding Memory and Thread Safety Practices and Issues in Real-World Rust Programs
qin20.text: B. Qin, Y. Chen, Z. Yu, L. Song, Y. Zhang. PLDI 2020.

rustbelt18.title: RustBelt: Securing the Foundations of the Rust Programming Language
rustbelt18.text: R. Jung, J.-H. Jourdan, R. Krebbers, D. Dreyer. POPL 2018 (PACMPL vol. 2).

stackedborrows20.title: Stacked Borrows: An Aliasing Model for Rust
stackedborrows20.text: R. Jung, H.-H. Dang, J. Kang, D. Dreyer. POPL 2020 (PACMPL vol. 4). The aliasing discipline Miri checks by default.

verus23.title: Verus: Verifying Rust Programs using Linear Ghost Types
verus23.text: A. Lattuada, T. Hance, C. Cho, M. Brun, I. Subasinghe, Y. Zhou, J. Howell, B. Parno, C. Hawblitzel. OOPSLA 2023.

z3.title: Z3: An Efficient SMT Solver
z3.text: L. de Moura, N. Bjørner. TACAS 2008. The solver behind every proof result reported here.

ctverif16.title: Verifying Constant-Time Implementations
ctverif16.text: J. B. Almeida, M. Barbosa, G. Barthe, F. Dupressoir, M. Emmi. USENIX Security 2016. Reduces constant-time, a relational property, to a safety property of a product program.

jasmin17.title: Jasmin: High-Assurance and High-Speed Cryptography
jasmin17.text: J. B. Almeida, M. Barbosa, G. Barthe, A. Blot, B. Grégoire, V. Laporte, T. Oliveira, et al. ACM CCS 2017.

fact19.title: FaCT: A DSL for Timing-Sensitive Computation
fact19.text: S. Cauligi, G. Soeller, B. Johannesmeyer, F. Brown, R. S. Wahby, J. Renner, B. Grégoire, G. Barthe, R. Jhala, D. Stefan. PLDI 2019.

compcertct.title: Formal Verification of a Constant-Time Preserving C Compiler
compcertct.text: G. Barthe, S. Blazy, B. Grégoire, R. Hutin, V. Laporte, D. Pichardie, A. Trieu. POPL 2020 (PACMPL vol. 4). Addresses the artefact half of the problem: the back end chooses the machine code after the prover has finished.

mytkowicz09.title: Producing Wrong Data Without Doing Anything Obviously Wrong!
mytkowicz09.text: T. Mytkowicz, A. Diwan, M. Hauswirth, P. F. Sweeney. ASPLOS 2009. Measurement bias from environment size and link order, large enough to invert conclusions.

stabilizer13.title: STABILIZER: Statistically Sound Performance Evaluation
stabilizer13.text: C. Curtsinger, E. D. Berger. ASPLOS 2013. Repeatedly re-randomises code and data layout so layout effects can be treated statistically.

userstudy25.title: Translating C To Rust: Lessons from a User Study
userstudy25.text: R. Li, B. Wang, T. Li, P. Saxena, A. Kundu. “Translating C To Rust: Lessons from a User Study.” Network and Distributed System Security (NDSS) Symposium 2025. 33 participants produced 31 pure-safe-Rust translations of 8 C programs of 322–536 lines. Page citations here are to the authors' extended version, arXiv:2411.14174v2, whose pagination differs from the proceedings.

taxdc16.title: TaxDC: A Taxonomy of Non-Deterministic Concurrency Bugs in Datacenter Distributed Systems
taxdc16.text: T. Leesatapornwongsa, J. F. Lukman, S. Lu, H. S. Gunawi. ASPLOS 2016. A taxonomy of 104 distributed concurrency bugs; cited here for the shape of its findings list, not its subject.

skel25.title: Program Skeletons for Automated Program Translation
skel25.text: B. Wang, T. Li, R. Li, U. Mathur, P. Saxena. Proc. ACM Program. Lang. 9, PLDI, Article 184 (2025). Decomposes cross-language translation into a mechanically translated skeleton plus separately synthesised fragments.
